account: It is noon on day 1, and I am home for my scheduled lunch. The unusual news today is a vaguely reported bridge or port change discussed at the bakery. Townsfolk named the baker, freight, builder and innkeeper as present. My neighbour also heard this report, but explicitly did not know the details or whether anything actually changed. I have not seen a change myself. The neighbour separately told me that the baker, freight and innkeeper were coordinating a bread order last evening. These discussions might be connected—perhaps arranging bread supplies and transport—but that is only a possibility, not something established. During my ten-o'clock mill inspection I saw 74 hay bales and 108 emeralds in the mill stall; I did not establish anyone's grain needs or clarify the crossing report, and I did not find the baker at the bakery. Tonight at eighteen I have a confirmed great hall meeting about the innkeeper's community hospitality matter. The appointment says I should attend alone with no preparation needed, and the secretary will remind and escort me. That could relate to the bread coordination, but I do not know that it does. Ordinary business continues: the secretary is receiving council correspondence for my thirteen-o'clock office session, although none had been handed over earlier this morning. The town accounts remain unresolved because the records custodian and ledger location have not been identified. I also have tea with my neighbour at the east-bank cottage at fifteen, office hours at sixteen-thirty, and home at nineteen.
